title: Federal Reserve holds interest rates steady as midterm elections loom
summary: The Federal Reserve left its benchmark rate at 3.75% to 4% on October 28, its last decision before the midterms, saying it wants more data even though inflation hit 3.7% in September. Chair Kevin Warsh described growth as strong while job gains have slowed sharply, leaving the Fed caught between rising prices and a softening labour market. Traders now put high odds on a December hike, bank research notes weigh the risks of overtightening versus lost credibility, and President Trump renewed his demands for lower rates.
focus: Shadow the correspondent's opening explanation of what the Fed decided and why, then her closing look ahead to the December meeting; both are short, clearly paced explainer passages.
